label: The push-out curve
subgoals: Sweep the data-to-clock skew and measure clock-to-q
Identify the flat nominal region and the steep push-out region
Recognize that setup needs a chosen criterion on a continuous curve

label: The push-out criterion
subgoals: Compute the clock-to-q limit from the nominal value and percentage
Find the smallest skew whose clock-to-q stays within the limit
Search for that skew by bisection with one transient per probe

label: Why the criterion matters downstream
subgoals: Add skew and clock-to-q to get the data-to-output delay
Find the skew that minimizes that sum on the curve
Treat the criterion as a core definition because it shifts every table
